info.short_description: FIPS code: 5-digit county code in county_determinants.parquet, and 2-digit state code or 00 for national in state_determinants.parquet. Includes Puerto Rico and, for AHRF, Guam and the U.S. Virgin Islands.

Year-end date (YYYY-12-31) of the data vintage. Each source has its own vintage(s): HUD CHAS 2022 (ACS 5-year), AHRF 1999-2025, BLS LAUS 2025, USDA Food Access Research Atlas 2019, Census ACS 5-year 2019-2024, Census SAHIE and SAIPE 2024, Census urban/rural allocation 2020 (2020 Decennial), Census OQM 2020.
Identifier of the measure in this row; the name matches the source column in the contributing source's standard file.

info.long_name: Households with 1+ of 4 Severe Housing Problems (HUD CHAS)
info.short_description: Share of occupied housing units with at least 1 of 4 severe housing problems.
info.long_description: Percentage of occupied housing units (owner + renter) with 1 or more of 4 severe housing problems: lacks complete kitchen facilities, lacks complete plumbing facilities, more than 1.5 persons per room, or cost burden greater than 50%. Computed from HUD's Comprehensive Housing Affordability Strategy (CHAS) data, Table 2 (Tenure by Severe Housing Unit Problems by Household Income by Race), as (T2_est3 + T2_est76) / T2_est1 -- the pre-combined owner and renter 'has 1+ severe problems, all incomes, all races' subtotals divided by total occupied units. Released on the ACS 5-year cycle with no fixed schedule. Intended as the direct-source input behind PopHIVE/us-rates' chr_severe_housing_problems measure.
info.statement: In {location}, {value} of households have a severe housing problem.

info.long_name: Health Professional Shortage Area Designation — Primary Care
info.short_description: Federal HPSA designation indicating primary care provider shortages.
info.long_description: Health Professional Shortage Area (HPSA) designation for primary medical care, assigned by HRSA. A value of 1 indicates a whole-county shortage area; 2 indicates a partial-county shortage area; 0 or missing indicates no shortage designation.
info.statement: In {location}, the primary care HPSA designation is {value}.

info.long_name: Health Professional Shortage Area Designation — Dental
info.short_description: Federal HPSA designation indicating dental provider shortages.
info.long_description: Health Professional Shortage Area (HPSA) designation for dental care, assigned by HRSA. A value of 1 indicates a whole-county shortage area; 2 indicates a partial-county shortage area; 0 or missing indicates no shortage designation.
info.statement: In {location}, the dental HPSA designation is {value}.

info.long_name: Health Professional Shortage Area Designation — Mental Health
info.short_description: Federal HPSA designation indicating mental health provider shortages.
info.long_description: Health Professional Shortage Area (HPSA) designation for mental health care, assigned by HRSA. A value of 1 indicates a whole-county shortage area; 2 indicates a partial-county shortage area; 0 or missing indicates no shortage designation.
info.statement: In {location}, the mental health HPSA designation is {value}.

info.long_name: USDA Rural-Urban Continuum Code
info.short_description: USDA rural-urban continuum code classifying counties from metro to rural (1–9).
info.long_description: USDA Economic Research Service Rural-Urban Continuum Code. Codes 1–3 are metropolitan counties (by population size of metro area); codes 4–9 are nonmetropolitan counties ranging from urbanized adjacent to metro areas (4) to completely rural or less than 2,500 urban population not adjacent to a metro area (9). The AHRF technical documentation lists this variable with 2013 vintage codes, so check the vintage before using it for trends.
info.statement: In {location}, the rural-urban continuum code is {value}.

info.long_name: Non-Federal Primary Care Physicians in Patient Care (Excluding Residents)
info.short_description: Count of non-federal primary care physicians (MDs and DOs) in patient care roles, excluding hospital residents.
info.long_description: Number of non-federal primary care physicians (including both MDs and DOs) actively in patient care, excluding hospital residents and those age 75 or older. Primary care includes general practice, family medicine, general internal medicine, general pediatrics, and obstetrics/gynecology. Source: AMA Physician Masterfile compiled by HRSA.
info.statement: In {location}, there are {value} primary care physicians in patient care.

info.long_name: Non-Federal Medical Doctors in Total Patient Care
info.short_description: Count of non-federal MDs across all specialties in patient care roles.
info.long_description: Total number of non-federal medical doctors (MDs) in patient care roles across all specialties. Includes office-based, hospital-based, and other patient care settings. Does not include federal physicians or DOs. Source: AMA Physician Masterfile compiled by HRSA.
info.statement: In {location}, there are {value} MDs in patient care.

info.long_name: Non-Federal Psychiatrists (Total)
info.short_description: Count of non-federal adult psychiatrists.
info.long_description: Total number of non-federal psychiatrists (MDs), across all activity categories (patient care, administration, teaching, research). AHRF reports child and adolescent psychiatrists as a separate variable, which this pipeline does not pull. Source: AMA Physician Masterfile compiled by HRSA.
info.statement: In {location}, there are {value} psychiatrists.

info.long_name: Dentists with Active National Provider Identifier
info.short_description: Count of dentists with an active NPI in the county.
info.long_description: Number of dentists with an active National Provider Identifier (NPI) in the county, derived from the CMS National Plan and Provider Enumeration System (NPPES). Includes all dental specialties.
info.statement: In {location}, there are {value} dentists with an active NPI.

info.long_name: Total Hospitals
info.short_description: Total number of hospitals in the county.
info.long_description: Total count of hospitals in the county across all types (short-term general, specialty, long-term, psychiatric, rehabilitation, and other). Source: American Hospital Association (AHA) Annual Survey compiled by HRSA.
info.statement: In {location}, there are {value} hospitals.

info.long_name: Critical Access Hospitals (Count)
info.short_description: Number of Medicare-certified critical access hospitals in the county.
info.long_description: Count of hospitals certified as Critical Access Hospitals (CAH) by CMS. CAHs are rural hospitals with 25 or fewer acute care inpatient beds, located more than 35 miles from another hospital, that receive enhanced Medicare reimbursement to maintain access to care in rural areas. Source: AHA Annual Survey compiled by HRSA.
info.statement: In {location}, there are {value} critical access hospitals.

info.long_name: Total County Population (LAPI Estimate)
info.short_description: Total county resident population (LAPI estimate).
info.long_description: Total county resident population, from the Local Area Personal Income (LAPI) estimates that HRSA carries in AHRF as the 'Population (Persons)' variable. The AHRF also includes separate Census County Population Estimates, which this pipeline does not pull.
info.statement: In {location}, the estimated total population is {value}.

info.long_name: Percentage of Days with Good Air Quality
info.short_description: Percentage of measured days rated 'Good' by EPA Air Quality Index.
info.long_description: Percentage of measured days in the county rated 'Good' (AQI 0-50) on the EPA Air Quality Index report, as carried in AHRF. Counties with no air quality monitoring data have no value.
info.statement: In {location}, {value}% of measured days had good air quality.

info.long_name: Annual Average Fine Particulate Matter (PM2.5) Concentration
info.short_description: Annual average PM2.5 concentration (μg/m³) from EPA monitoring data.
info.long_description: Annual average ambient fine particulate matter (PM2.5) concentration in micrograms per cubic meter, from the CDC Environmental Public Health Tracking Network as carried in AHRF. In the 2025 release, values exist only for 2019 and 2020. Counties without monitoring stations may have NA values.
info.statement: In {location}, the annual average PM2.5 concentration is {value} μg/m³.

info.long_name: Population Density per Square Mile
info.short_description: County population density per square mile from Census data.
info.long_description: Resident population per square mile of total county area, from the 2020 Census redistricting data as carried in AHRF. The AHRF also carries 2010 values for earlier data years.
info.statement: In {location}, the population density is {value} persons per square mile.

info.long_name: Actual Medicare Fee-for-Service Per Capita Expenditure
info.short_description: Actual Medicare FFS per capita spending for county residents.
info.long_description: Actual (not price-standardized) Medicare fee-for-service per capita expenditures for county residents enrolled in traditional Medicare. Reflects local healthcare prices, service intensity, and enrollment patterns. Source: CMS Medicare Geographic Variation data, as carried in AHRF.
info.statement: In {location}, Medicare FFS per capita spending is ${value}.

info.long_name: Emergency Department Visits per 1,000 Medicare FFS Beneficiaries
info.short_description: County ED visit rate among traditional Medicare fee-for-service enrollees.
info.long_description: Number of emergency department visits per 1,000 Medicare fee-for-service (FFS) beneficiaries residing in the county. Captures acute care utilization and may reflect access barriers, disease burden, or care coordination quality. Source: CMS Medicare Geographic Variation data, as carried in AHRF.
info.statement: In {location}, there are {value} ED visits per 1,000 Medicare FFS beneficiaries.
info.unit: ED visits per 1,000 Medicare FFS beneficiaries

info.long_name: Unemployment Rate, Ages 16 and Older (BLS LAUS)
info.short_description: Share of the civilian labor force ages 16+ that is unemployed but seeking work.
info.long_description: Annual average county, state, and national unemployment rate. County and state estimates come from the Bureau of Labor Statistics' Local Area Unemployment Statistics (LAUS) program, series measure code 03 (not seasonally adjusted; LAUS county and state series are never seasonally adjusted); the national estimate comes from BLS's standard CPS-based unemployment rate series (LNU04000000), since LAUS itself publishes no national series. LAUS estimates are model-based (signal-plus-noise time-series model for states, Handbook procedures for labor market areas, disaggregation for counties) and are re-benchmarked in later years against updated QCEW/population controls, so a live pull will not always exactly match a value captured at an earlier point in time for the same reference year. LAUS's state-equivalent coverage includes the 50 states, DC, and Puerto Rico, but not American Samoa, Guam, the Northern Mariana Islands, the U.S. Virgin Islands, or the Minor Outlying Islands. Intended as the direct-source input behind PopHIVE/us-rates' chr_unemployment measure, which uses the same LAUS rate series with no further CHR&R-side adjustment.
info.statement: In {location}, {value} of the labor force is unemployed.

info.long_name: Low-Income and Low Food-Access Population (USDA Food Environment Atlas)
info.short_description: Share of county population that is low-income and lives more than 1 mile (urban) or 10 miles (rural) from a grocery store.
info.long_description: Percentage of the county population that is both low-income (at or below 200% of the federal poverty line) and has limited access to a grocery store, from the USDA Economic Research Service's Food Environment Atlas (variable PCT_LACCESS_LOWI19). This is USDA's own county-level aggregation of tract-level data from the separate Food Access Research Atlas. The underlying low-access variables were last updated for 2019 and have not been refreshed since, despite newer overall Atlas releases. Three Alaska boroughs (Chugach 02063, Copper River 02066, Valdez-Cordova 02261) are NA in the source due to a FIPS reorganization. Intended as the direct-source input behind PopHIVE/us-rates' chr_limited_access_to_healthy_foods measure -- County Health Rankings & Roadmaps is itself still using this same 2019 vintage.
info.statement: In {location}, {value} of the population is low-income with limited access to healthy food.

info.long_name: Median Earnings for Full-Time, Year-Round Workers
info.short_description: Median earnings for full-time, year-round workers in dollars.
info.long_description: Median earnings for full-time, year-round civilian workers aged 16 and older in current dollars, derived from ACS Table B20017.
info.statement: In {location}, the median earnings for workers is ${value}.

info.long_name: Median Household Income
info.short_description: Median household income in the past 12 months in dollars.
info.long_description: Median household income in current dollars, including all sources of income for all household members, derived from ACS Table B19013.
info.statement: In {location}, the median household income is ${value}.

info.long_name: Per Capita Income
info.short_description: Mean income per person in dollars.
info.long_description: Per capita income computed by dividing total aggregate income by the total population, derived from ACS Table B19301.
info.statement: In {location}, the per capita income is ${value}.

info.long_name: Share of Aggregate Household Income: Lowest (First) Quintile
info.short_description: Share of aggregate household income received by the lowest 20% of households.
info.long_description: Proportion of total aggregate household income received by households in the lowest income quintile, derived from ACS Table B19082.
info.statement: In {location}, the lowest income quintile receives {value} of total income.

info.long_name: Share of Aggregate Household Income: Second Quintile
info.short_description: Share of aggregate household income received by the second 20% of households.
info.long_description: Proportion of total aggregate household income received by households in the second income quintile, derived from ACS Table B19082.
info.statement: In {location}, the second income quintile receives {value} of total income.

info.long_name: Share of Aggregate Household Income: Third Quintile
info.short_description: Share of aggregate household income received by the middle 20% of households.
info.long_description: Proportion of total aggregate household income received by households in the third (middle) income quintile, derived from ACS Table B19082.
info.statement: In {location}, the middle income quintile receives {value} of total income.

info.long_name: Share of Aggregate Household Income: Fourth Quintile
info.short_description: Share of aggregate household income received by the fourth 20% of households.
info.long_description: Proportion of total aggregate household income received by households in the fourth income quintile, derived from ACS Table B19082.
info.statement: In {location}, the fourth income quintile receives {value} of total income.

info.long_name: Share of Aggregate Household Income: Highest (Fifth) Quintile
info.short_description: Share of aggregate household income received by the highest 20% of households.
info.long_description: Proportion of total aggregate household income received by households in the highest income quintile, derived from ACS Table B19082.
info.statement: In {location}, the highest income quintile receives {value} of total income.

info.long_name: Share of Aggregate Household Income: Top 5%
info.short_description: Share of aggregate household income received by the top 5% of households.
info.long_description: Proportion of total aggregate household income received by households in the top 5%, derived from ACS Table B19082.
info.statement: In {location}, the top 5% of households receive {value} of total income.

info.long_name: Gini Index of Income Inequality
info.short_description: Measure of household income inequality (0=perfect equality, 1=maximum inequality).
info.long_description: The Gini index measures the degree of income inequality among households, derived from ACS Table B19083. A value of 0 represents perfect equality; 1 represents maximum inequality. The ACS Gini is based on household income.
info.statement: In {location}, the Gini index of income inequality is {value}.

info.long_name: Income Quintile Share Ratio (S80/S20)
info.short_description: Ratio of income share of the top 20% to the bottom 20% of households.
info.long_description: The S80/S20 ratio is computed as the share of aggregate income held by the top quintile divided by the share held by the lowest quintile, derived from ACS Table B19081. A higher ratio indicates greater income inequality.
info.statement: In {location}, the income quintile share ratio (S80/S20) is {value}.

info.long_name: Poverty Rate (Below 100% Federal Poverty Level)
info.short_description: Share of the population with income below the federal poverty level.
info.long_description: Proportion of the population with family income below the federal poverty threshold, derived from ACS Table B17001.
info.statement: In {location}, {value} of the population lives below the poverty level.

info.long_name: Deep Poverty Rate (Below 50% of Federal Poverty Level)
info.short_description: Share of the population with income below 50% of the federal poverty level.
info.long_description: Proportion of the population with income below 50% of the federal poverty threshold (deep poverty), derived from ACS Table C17002.
info.statement: In {location}, {value} of the population is in deep poverty (below 50% of the poverty level).

info.long_name: Near-Poverty Rate (Below 150% of Federal Poverty Level)
info.short_description: Share of the population with income below 150% of the federal poverty level.
info.long_description: Proportion of the population with income below 150% of the federal poverty threshold, derived from ACS Table C17002.
info.statement: In {location}, {value} of the population has income below 150% of the poverty level.

info.long_name: Low-Income Rate (Below 200% of Federal Poverty Level)
info.short_description: Share of the population with income below 200% of the federal poverty level.
info.long_description: Proportion of the population with income below 200% of the federal poverty threshold, derived from ACS Table C17002.
info.statement: In {location}, {value} of the population has income below 200% of the poverty level.

info.long_name: Housing Cost Burden Rate (Spending 30%+ of Income on Housing)
info.short_description: Share of households spending 30% or more of income on housing costs.
info.long_description: Proportion of occupied housing units where gross housing costs (rent or owner costs) exceed 30% of household income, derived from ACS Tables B25070 (renters) and B25091 (owners). Cost burden at 30% is the standard HUD threshold indicating housing affordability stress.
info.statement: In {location}, {value} of households are cost-burdened, spending 30%+ of income on housing.

info.long_name: Severe Housing Cost Burden Rate (Spending 50%+ of Income on Housing)
info.short_description: Share of households spending 50% or more of income on housing costs.
info.long_description: Proportion of occupied housing units where gross housing costs (rent or owner costs) exceed 50% of household income, derived from ACS Tables B25070 (renters) and B25091 (owners). Severe cost burden is a standard HUD threshold indicating serious housing affordability stress.
info.statement: In {location}, {value} of households are severely cost-burdened, spending 50%+ of income on housing.

info.long_name: Civilian Unemployment Rate
info.short_description: Share of the civilian labor force that is unemployed.
info.long_description: Proportion of the civilian labor force (aged 16+) that is unemployed and actively seeking work, derived from ACS Table B23001. The numerator includes unemployed civilians; the denominator includes all civilians in the labor force.
info.statement: In {location}, {value} of the civilian labor force is unemployed.

info.long_name: High School Graduation Rate (Adults 25+)
info.short_description: Share of adults aged 25+ who have at least a high school diploma or equivalent.
info.long_description: Proportion of the population aged 25 and older who have completed high school (including equivalency), derived from ACS Table B15002. Includes all levels of educational attainment at or above high school.
info.statement: In {location}, {value} of adults aged 25+ have at least a high school diploma.

info.long_name: Higher Education Attainment Rate (Adults 25+)
info.short_description: Share of adults aged 25+ who have attended any college or higher.
info.long_description: Proportion of the population aged 25 and older who have some college, an associate degree, a bachelor's degree, or a graduate/professional degree, derived from ACS Table B15002.
info.statement: In {location}, {value} of adults aged 25+ have attended college or obtained a higher degree.

info.long_name: Opportunity Youth Rate (Ages 16–24, Not in School or Work)
info.short_description: Share of youth aged 16–24 who are neither enrolled in school nor employed.
info.long_description: Proportion of the population aged 16–24 who are not enrolled in school and not employed (sometimes called 'disconnected youth' or 'opportunity youth'), derived from ACS Table B14005.
info.statement: In {location}, {value} of youth aged 16–24 are neither in school nor employed.

info.long_name: Limited English Proficiency Rate
info.short_description: Share of the population aged 5+ who speak English less than 'very well'.
info.long_description: Proportion of the population aged 5 and older who speak a language other than English at home and speak English less than 'very well' (limited English proficiency), derived from ACS Table B16004.
info.statement: In {location}, {value} of residents aged 5+ have limited English proficiency.

info.long_name: Health Insurance Uninsured Rate
info.short_description: Share of the civilian noninstitutionalized population without health insurance.
info.long_description: Proportion of the civilian noninstitutionalized population with no health insurance coverage of any type, derived from ACS Table B27001.
info.statement: In {location}, {value} of the population is uninsured.

info.long_name: Medicaid/Means-Tested Public Coverage Rate
info.short_description: Share of the civilian noninstitutionalized population covered by Medicaid or other means-tested public insurance.
info.long_description: Proportion of the civilian noninstitutionalized population with Medicaid or other means-tested public health insurance coverage, derived from ACS Subject Table S2704. Note: not available for all geographies or all vintage years.
info.statement: In {location}, {value} of the population is covered by Medicaid.

info.long_name: Medicare Coverage Rate
info.short_description: Share of the civilian noninstitutionalized population covered by Medicare.
info.long_description: Proportion of the civilian noninstitutionalized population with Medicare health insurance coverage, derived from ACS Subject Table S2704. Note: not available for all geographies or all vintage years.
info.statement: In {location}, {value} of the population is covered by Medicare.

info.long_name: Owner-Occupied Housing Rate
info.short_description: Share of occupied housing units that are owner-occupied.
info.long_description: Proportion of occupied housing units that are owner-occupied (homeownership rate), derived from ACS Table B25003.
info.statement: In {location}, {value} of occupied housing units are owner-occupied.

info.long_name: Mobile Home Housing Rate
info.short_description: Share of housing units that are mobile homes or trailers.
info.long_description: Proportion of all housing units that are mobile homes, manufactured homes, or trailers, derived from ACS Table B25024.
info.statement: In {location}, {value} of housing units are mobile homes.

info.long_name: Crowded Housing Rate (More Than 1 Person per Room)
info.short_description: Share of occupied housing units with more than 1 person per room.
info.long_description: Proportion of occupied housing units with more than 1 person per room (a standard indicator of housing crowding), derived from ACS Table B25014.
info.statement: In {location}, {value} of housing units are crowded (more than 1 person per room).

info.long_name: Rate of Housing Units Lacking Complete Plumbing Facilities
info.short_description: Share of housing units without complete indoor plumbing.
info.long_description: Proportion of occupied housing units that lack complete plumbing facilities (hot and cold running water, a bathtub or shower, and a flush toilet), derived from ACS Table B25048.
info.statement: In {location}, {value} of housing units lack complete plumbing facilities.

info.long_name: Rate of Occupied Housing Units Without Telephone Service
info.short_description: Share of occupied housing units without telephone service.
info.long_description: Proportion of occupied housing units with no telephone service available (neither landline nor cellular), derived from ACS Table B25043.
info.statement: In {location}, {value} of households have no telephone service.

info.long_name: Group Quarters Population Rate
info.short_description: Share of the total population living in group quarters (prisons, dorms, nursing homes, etc.).
info.long_description: Proportion of the total population residing in group quarters (e.g., correctional facilities, college dormitories, nursing facilities, military barracks), derived from ACS Tables B26001 and B01001.
info.statement: In {location}, {value} of the population lives in group quarters.

info.long_name: Household Broadband (High-Speed) Internet Subscription Rate
info.short_description: Share of households with a broadband internet subscription.
info.long_description: Proportion of occupied housing units that have a broadband (high-speed) internet subscription, derived from ACS Table B28002. Includes cable, fiber, DSL, satellite, and fixed wireless connections.
info.statement: In {location}, {value} of households have a broadband internet subscription.

info.long_name: Rate of Households Without Internet Access
info.short_description: Share of households without any internet access.
info.long_description: Proportion of occupied housing units with no internet subscription of any kind, derived from ACS Table B28002.
info.statement: In {location}, {value} of households have no internet access.

info.long_name: Public Transportation Commute Rate
info.short_description: Share of workers who commute primarily by public transportation.
info.long_description: Proportion of workers aged 16 and older who use public transportation (excluding taxicab) as their primary means of commuting to work, derived from ACS Table B08301.
info.statement: In {location}, {value} of workers commute primarily by public transportation.

info.long_name: Single-Parent Household Rate
info.short_description: Share of family households headed by a single parent with children.
info.long_description: Proportion of family households that are headed by a single parent (male or female householder, no spouse present) with children under 18, derived from ACS Table B11012.
info.statement: In {location}, {value} of family households are headed by a single parent.

info.long_name: SNAP (Food Stamp) Participation Rate
info.short_description: Share of households receiving SNAP (food stamp) benefits.
info.long_description: Proportion of households that received Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP, formerly food stamps) benefits in the past 12 months, derived from ACS Table B22003.
info.statement: In {location}, {value} of households receive SNAP benefits.

info.long_name: Percent of County Population Living in Urban Areas (2020 Census)
info.short_description: Share of county population residing in Census-defined urban areas.
info.long_description: Proportion of a county's 2020 Census population living within Census-defined urban areas (urbanized areas and urban clusters combined). Derived from the 2020 Census Urban Area to County Allocation File by summing each county's urban-area population share across all intersecting urban areas. Counties with no urban area are assigned 0. Values are 2020 Census vintage and do not vary by year.
info.statement: In {location}, {value} of the population lives in urban areas.

info.long_name: Percent of County Land Area Classified as Urban (2020 Census)
info.short_description: Share of county land area within Census-defined urban areas.
info.long_description: Proportion of a county's total land area that falls within Census-defined urban areas (urbanized areas and urban clusters combined). Derived from the 2020 Census Urban Area to County Allocation File. Counties with no urban area are assigned 0. Values are 2020 Census vintage and do not vary by year.
info.statement: In {location}, {value} of the land area is classified as urban.

info.long_name: Percent of County Housing Units in Urban Areas (2020 Census)
info.short_description: Share of county housing units located in Census-defined urban areas.
info.long_description: Proportion of a county's 2020 Census housing units located within Census-defined urban areas (urbanized areas and urban clusters combined). Derived from the 2020 Census Urban Area to County Allocation File. Counties with no urban area are assigned 0. Values are 2020 Census vintage and do not vary by year.
info.statement: In {location}, {value} of housing units are in urban areas.

info.long_name: Percent Uninsured, Under Age 65 (SAHIE)
info.short_description: Share of county population under age 65 without health insurance.
info.long_description: Small Area Health Insurance Estimates (SAHIE) percent uninsured for AGECAT=0 (Under 65 years), all incomes/races/sexes combined. Intended as the Census-native input behind PopHIVE/us-rates' chr_uninsured measure.
info.statement: In {location}, {value} of the population under 65 is uninsured.

info.long_name: Percent Uninsured, Ages 18-64 (SAHIE)
info.short_description: Share of county residents ages 18-64 without health insurance.
info.long_description: Small Area Health Insurance Estimates (SAHIE) percent uninsured for AGECAT=1 (18 to 64), all incomes/races/sexes combined. Intended as the Census-native input behind PopHIVE/us-rates' chr_uninsured_adults measure.

info.long_name: 2020 Census Self-Response Rate (Operational Quality Metrics)
info.short_description: Share of addresses that self-responded to the 2020 Census, among all addresses (not just those invited to self-respond).
info.long_description: From the Census Bureau's 2020 Census Operational Quality Metrics (Release 4), the percent of all addresses in the county resolved via self-response (by internet, phone, or mail) rather than nonresponse followup. Static 2020 vintage; will not update again until the 2030 Census. Intended as the Census-native input behind PopHIVE/us-rates' chr_census_participation measure.
info.statement: In {location}, {value} of addresses self-responded to the 2020 Census.

info.long_name: Value of the determinant measure identified by outcome_name
info.short_description: Value for the measure identified by the `outcome_name` column. Units differ by measure: HUD, BLS, USDA and every Census rate or share are proportions (0-1); AHRF measures are counts, rates, codes, or percentages; the remaining Census measures are dollars, ratios or index values as documented for each source variable.
info.long_description: Value for the measure identified by the `outcome_name` column, taken unchanged from the contributing source's standard file (see each level's source documentation for definition and unit). Rows with missing values are dropped, so sparse AHRF measures have fewer rows than the full county x year grid. Note that `ahrf_rural_urban_code` is a categorical USDA Rural-Urban Continuum Code (1-9) stored numerically. Every Census rate and share in this file is a proportion on the same 0-1 scale as the HUD, BLS and USDA measures, so they are directly comparable; this includes the income-quintile shares (`acs_INL`, `acs_INM`, `acs_INN`, `acs_INO`, `acs_INP`), which sum to 1 within a geography-year, while `acs_INQ` is the top-5% share and is a subset of the highest quintile rather than a sixth additive category. Three Census groups are not proportions: `acs_OWS` is an unbounded S80/S20 ratio, `acs_GNI` is a 0-1 Gini index, and `acs_INB`, `acs_INC`, `acs_PCI` and `saipe_median_household_income` are nominal dollars, not inflation-adjusted, so they are not comparable across vintages without deflating.

info.long_name: Unemployment Rate, Ages 16 and Older (BLS LAUS)
info.short_description: Share of the civilian labor force ages 16+ that is unemployed but seeking work.
info.long_description: Annual average county, state, and national unemployment rate. County and state estimates come from the Bureau of Labor Statistics' Local Area Unemployment Statistics (LAUS) program, series measure code 03 (not seasonally adjusted; LAUS county and state series are never seasonally adjusted); the national estimate comes from BLS's standard CPS-based unemployment rate series (LNU04000000), since LAUS itself publishes no national series. LAUS estimates are model-based (signal-plus-noise time-series model for states, Handbook procedures for labor market areas, disaggregation for counties) and are re-benchmarked in later years against updated QCEW/population controls, so a live pull will not always exactly match a value captured at an earlier point in time for the same reference year. LAUS's state-equivalent coverage includes the 50 states, DC, and Puerto Rico, but not American Samoa, Guam, the Northern Mariana Islands, the U.S. Virgin Islands, or the Minor Outlying Islands. Intended as the direct-source input behind PopHIVE/us-rates' chr_unemployment measure, which uses the same LAUS rate series with no further CHR&R-side adjustment.
info.statement: In {location}, {value} of the labor force is unemployed.

info.long_name: Value of the determinant measure identified by outcome_name
info.short_description: Value for the measure identified by the `outcome_name` column. Units differ by measure: HUD, BLS, USDA and every Census rate or share are proportions (0-1); AHRF measures are counts, rates, codes, or percentages; the remaining Census measures are dollars, ratios or index values as documented for each source variable.
info.long_description: Value for the measure identified by the `outcome_name` column, taken unchanged from the contributing source's standard file (see each level's source documentation for definition and unit). Rows with missing values are dropped, so sparse AHRF measures have fewer rows than the full county x year grid. Note that `ahrf_rural_urban_code` is a categorical USDA Rural-Urban Continuum Code (1-9) stored numerically. Every Census rate and share in this file is a proportion on the same 0-1 scale as the HUD, BLS and USDA measures, so they are directly comparable; this includes the income-quintile shares (`acs_INL`, `acs_INM`, `acs_INN`, `acs_INO`, `acs_INP`), which sum to 1 within a geography-year, while `acs_INQ` is the top-5% share and is a subset of the highest quintile rather than a sixth additive category. Three Census groups are not proportions: `acs_OWS` is an unbounded S80/S20 ratio, `acs_GNI` is a 0-1 Gini index, and `acs_INB`, `acs_INC`, `acs_PCI` and `saipe_median_household_income` are nominal dollars, not inflation-adjusted, so they are not comparable across vintages without deflating.

info.long_name: Unemployment Rate, Ages 16 and Older (BLS LAUS)
info.short_description: Share of the civilian labor force ages 16+ that is unemployed but seeking work.
info.long_description: Annual average county, state, and national unemployment rate. County and state estimates come from the Bureau of Labor Statistics' Local Area Unemployment Statistics (LAUS) program, series measure code 03 (not seasonally adjusted; LAUS county and state series are never seasonally adjusted); the national estimate comes from BLS's standard CPS-based unemployment rate series (LNU04000000), since LAUS itself publishes no national series. LAUS estimates are model-based (signal-plus-noise time-series model for states, Handbook procedures for labor market areas, disaggregation for counties) and are re-benchmarked in later years against updated QCEW/population controls, so a live pull will not always exactly match a value captured at an earlier point in time for the same reference year. LAUS's state-equivalent coverage includes the 50 states, DC, and Puerto Rico, but not American Samoa, Guam, the Northern Mariana Islands, the U.S. Virgin Islands, or the Minor Outlying Islands. Intended as the direct-source input behind PopHIVE/us-rates' chr_unemployment measure, which uses the same LAUS rate series with no further CHR&R-side adjustment.
info.statement: In {location}, {value} of the labor force is unemployed.

info.long_name: Low-Income and Low Food-Access Population (USDA Food Environment Atlas)

This is USDA's own county-level aggregation of tract-level data from the separate Food Access Research Atlas. The underlying low-access variables were last updated for 2019 and have not been refreshed since, despite newer overall Atlas releases. Three Alaska boroughs (Chugach 02063, Copper River 02066, Valdez-Cordova 02261) are NA in the source due to a FIPS reorganization. Intended as the direct-source input behind PopHIVE/us-rates' chr_limited_access_to_healthy_foods measure -- County Health Rankings & Roadmaps is itself still using this same 2019 vintage.

info.long_name: Unemployment Rate, Ages 16 and Older (BLS LAUS)
info.short_description: Share of the civilian labor force ages 16+ that is unemployed but seeking work.
info.long_description: Annual average county, state, and national unemployment rate. County and state estimates come from the Bureau of Labor Statistics' Local Area Unemployment Statistics (LAUS) program, series measure code 03 (not seasonally adjusted; LAUS county and state series are never seasonally adjusted); the national estimate comes from BLS's standard CPS-based unemployment rate series (LNU04000000), since LAUS itself publishes no national series. LAUS estimates are model-based (signal-plus-noise time-series model for states, Handbook procedures for labor market areas, disaggregation for counties) and are re-benchmarked in later years against updated QCEW/population controls, so a live pull will not always exactly match a value captured at an earlier point in time for the same reference year. LAUS's state-equivalent coverage includes the 50 states, DC, and Puerto Rico, but not American Samoa, Guam, the Northern Mariana Islands, the U.S. Virgin Islands, or the Minor Outlying Islands. Intended as the direct-source input behind PopHIVE/us-rates' chr_unemployment measure, which uses the same LAUS rate series with no further CHR&R-side adjustment.
info.statement: In {location}, {value} of the labor force is unemployed.

bundle_county_access/dist/county_determi.long_name: Value of the determinant measure identified by outcome_name
bundle_county_access/dist/county_determi.short_description: Value for the measure identified by the `outcome_name` column. Units differ by measure: HUD, BLS, USDA and every Census rate or share are proportions (0-1); AHRF measures are counts, rates, codes, or percentages; the remaining Census measures are dollars, ratios or index values as documented for each source variable.
bundle_county_access/dist/county_determi.long_description: Value for the measure identified by the `outcome_name` column, taken unchanged from the contributing source's standard file (see each level's source documentation for definition and unit). Rows with missing values are dropped, so sparse AHRF measures have fewer rows than the full county x year grid. Note that `ahrf_rural_urban_code` is a categorical USDA Rural-Urban Continuum Code (1-9) stored numerically. Every Census rate and share in this file is a proportion on the same 0-1 scale as the HUD, BLS and USDA measures, so they are directly comparable; this includes the income-quintile shares (`acs_INL`, `acs_INM`, `acs_INN`, `acs_INO`, `acs_INP`), which sum to 1 within a geography-year, while `acs_INQ` is the top-5% share and is a subset of the highest quintile rather than a sixth additive category. Three Census groups are not proportions: `acs_OWS` is an unbounded S80/S20 ratio, `acs_GNI` is a 0-1 Gini index, and `acs_INB`, `acs_INC`, `acs_PCI` and `saipe_median_household_income` are nominal dollars, not inflation-adjusted, so they are not comparable across vintages without deflating.

chr.name: County Health Rankings & Roadmaps
chr.organization: University of Wisconsin Population Health Institute
chr.location: County Health Rankings & Roadmaps Annual Data
chr.description: The County Health Rankings & Roadmaps (CHR&R) program, a collaboration between the Robert Wood Johnson Foundation and the University of Wisconsin Population Health Institute, ranks the health of nearly all counties in the nation. The annual rankings measure vital health factors including high school graduation rates, obesity, smoking, unemployment, access to healthy foods, the quality of air and water, income inequality, and teen births that influence how long and how well we live. Data are released annually and cover all U.S. counties. Raw data are publicly available through the Zenodo repository (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18157681) and span release years 2010 through the present.
